# Phase 11 gate report: the Phase 6 ceiling, re-measured on a replay that does not race

**Status: complete. The gate deliverables are done (tests, experiment, this report, commit).**

[Phase 6](PHASE_6.md) priced the one redesign the data pointed at — taking the residency decision
off the host — with a replay ablation, and found a ceiling of
1.11–1.16×.
[Phase 9](PHASE_9.md) §5 then found that the replay raced: the tier's pinned staging buffers were
refilled by the next layer before the previous layer's copy had read them, a hazard the normal path
never hits because its per-layer index sync drains every copy. The fix (commit `2be6251`) waits on a
CUDA event before a buffer is reused. That made the Phase 6 number suspect in one known direction,
and it has been quoted with a caveat in `FINDINGS.md` and the README since. This phase replaces the
caveat with a measurement.

## Gate checklist (CLAUDE.md rule 3)

- [x] **Tests run.** `pytest`, all passing, including the race test from Phase 9 (it stalls the
  device with `torch.cuda._sleep` so the host always runs ahead; it fails without the fix).
- [x] **Real experiment run.** `scripts/03_host_ceiling.py --config configs/phase11.yaml`, three
  independent runs (`--run-id 1..3`), launched detached from a worktree pinned at the commit under
  test, on an idle machine overnight; then `scripts/analyze_ceiling.py --phase phase11
  --compare-to phase5`.
- [x] **Phase doc written.** This file.
- [x] **Committed and pushed.**

## What changed, and what did not

`configs/phase11.yaml` is `configs/phase5.yaml` with the phase name changed: the same policies,
context (32,768 tokens), block size, decode length and warmup,
through the same script. **One claim in that config was wrong and is corrected in it:** Phase 6 ran
the script with a `--budgets 0.25 0.125 0.0625` override (its recorded `argv` says so), so this run's
75% and 50% conditions are additional. Every comparison with Phase 6 below is on the
6 conditions both phases measured. Two things
differ on purpose. The ceiling is now
3 independent runs rather than one, so it carries a
run-to-run range like every other latency in this study; and it ran with nothing else on the
machine. The expected direction was written into the config before the run: a correct replay must
wait for a copy the racy one skipped, so the ceiling should shrink or hold.

## 1. The ceiling

| Policy | Budget | Decode, ms/token | Replay, ms/token | Ceiling, Phase 6 (racy) | Ceiling, re-measured | Replay token agreement, Phase 6 | Replay token agreement, now | Same pairs fetched |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| CPU tier, int8 warm/cold (rung 8) | 75% | 31.1 | 26.2 | not measured | **1.187×** | not measured | 99.3% | yes |
| CPU tier, int8 warm/cold (rung 8) | 50% | 30.3 | 24.8 | not measured | **1.222×** | not measured | 100.0% | yes |
| CPU tier, int8 warm/cold (rung 8) | 25% | 60.3 | 54.9 | 1.113× | **1.097×** | 99.3% | 98.5% | yes |
| CPU tier, int8 warm/cold (rung 8) | 12.5% | 60.7 | 53.2 | 1.142× | **1.140×** | 99.3% | 98.5% | yes |
| CPU tier, int8 warm/cold (rung 8) | 6.25% | 60.1 | 53.4 | 1.164× | **1.124×** | 98.5% | 99.3% | yes |
| CPU tier, sync fetch (rung 6) | 75% | 29.8 | 23.8 | not measured | **1.251×** | not measured | 99.3% | yes |
| CPU tier, sync fetch (rung 6) | 50% | 31.2 | 26.2 | not measured | **1.194×** | not measured | 100.0% | yes |
| CPU tier, sync fetch (rung 6) | 25% | 52.7 | 46.3 | 1.152× | **1.139×** | 97.8% | 98.5% | yes |
| CPU tier, sync fetch (rung 6) | 12.5% | 53.6 | 48.2 | 1.161× | **1.112×** | 98.5% | 99.3% | yes |
| CPU tier, sync fetch (rung 6) | 6.25% | 53.5 | 46.8 | 1.164× | **1.144×** | 99.3% | 98.5% | yes |

**The ceiling shrank, as predicted, and not by much.** On the
6 shared conditions it is now
1.10–1.14×,
against Phase 6's
1.11–1.16×.
It is lower at **6 of
6**, keeping
69%–99%
of the speedup Phase 6 reported. That is the direction the race predicts — the racy replay skipped a
wait a correct one must pay — and the size says the race was a small part of the old number, not
most of it. Phase 6 was a single run, so the per-condition changes are individually within
run-to-run noise; the consistent direction is the finding, not any one ratio.

**Token agreement does not settle how much of Phase 6's disagreement was the race.** The replay
agrees with normal decode on
98.5%–100.0%
of tokens, against Phase 6's
97.8%–99.3%,
but condition by condition it moves in both directions, by a token or two out of the decode. That
is the size of the fast kernel's own nondeterminism (Phase 1: not bit-repeatable for single-query
decode, which is why quality is never measured on it), so the race's share of the old disagreement
is not measurable here. Fetched pairs match between the two passes in every condition, so the replay
does exactly the normal pass's gathers.

**The conclusion Phase 6 drew is unchanged.** Across all
3 runs and every budget, including the two new ones, a perfect
device-side decision is worth
1.10–1.25×.
The top of that range is at the new 75% and 50% budgets, above anything Phase 6 reported; not because
the decision costs more there — the milliseconds saved are similar — but because those budgets
decode about twice as fast, so the same saving is a larger fraction.
The fastest the replay ever decodes is
23.8 ms per token, still slower than the full cache's
18.8 ms. The redesign would narrow the tier's gap to
keeping KV in VRAM and never close it, which is what `FINDINGS.md` §4 says; the caveat
it carried can now be replaced by this number.

**Two instruments still agree.** The replay's saving differs from the rank-and-sync time counted
independently on normal decode by
-1.3 to
+1.0 ms per token, so the ceiling measures what it claims to.

**A note on the machine.** The runs were meant to be on an idle laptop, and mostly were, but the
system ran critically short of RAM at one point during them, and a few isolated repeats were slow (in run 1, the
full cache's second repeat was markedly slower than its other two). Every condition is a
median over three repeats and the ceiling pools three runs, so a single slow repeat does not move
it; the per-repeat logs are kept with the runs.
